stem: A stream was first started against a folder that already held a year of history, and the backfill came through as expected. Months later the team sets the option that governs pre-existing files to false, restarts, and sees no change at all.

option_texts.A: The option is evaluated only on the very first start, so a restart cannot change it
option_texts.B: The option needs the checkpoint cleared as well, after which the restart would apply
option_texts.C: The option applies only in notification mode, and this stream lists the directory
option_texts.D: The option was overridden, because a change to the folder contents outranks it

drill_answer_short: cloudFiles.includeExistingFiles is evaluated only when the stream starts for the first time; later changes have no effect
decision_hinge: The cloudFiles.includeExistingFiles option is evaluated only when you start a stream for the first time, and changing this option after restarting the stream has no effect.

plausible_options.B: restarts, and sees no change at all

eliminated_by.C: A stream was first started against a folder that already held a year of history
eliminated_by.D: the team sets the option that governs pre-existing files to false

distractor_traps.B: T3: confusable sibling - a fresh checkpoint is a new first start, but the option itself still never re-applies to this stream
distractor_traps.C: T1: fabricated - the option is not limited to one discovery mode
distractor_traps.D: T5: common misconception - file age does not override a stream option

stem: A stream infers its shape from JSON files that hold obvious numbers and dates, yet every field lands in the silver table as text. Nothing downstream is casting anything, and the team wants the reason before they add casts everywhere.

option_texts.A: Inference is off entirely, so the reader falls back to one text column per field
option_texts.B: Exact column types are not inferred by default, so JSON fields come through as strings
option_texts.C: Inference reads only the first file, which happened to quote all of its values
option_texts.D: The target table was created with text columns, so the values were cast on write

drill_answer_short: cloudFiles.inferColumnTypes defaults to false, so columns are inferred as strings for JSON and CSV
decision_hinge: The cloudFiles.inferColumnTypes option defaults to false, and by default columns are inferred as strings when inferring JSON and CSV datasets.

plausible_options.D: every field lands in the silver table as text

eliminated_by.A: A stream infers its shape from JSON files that hold obvious numbers and dates
eliminated_by.C: the team wants the reason before they add casts everywhere

distractor_traps.A: T3: confusable sibling - inference is running, it simply does not resolve exact types by default
distractor_traps.C: T5: common misconception - sampling breadth is not what makes the columns text
distractor_traps.D: T2: scope error - the question is how the source was read, not how the target was declared

stem: A producer rewrites yesterday's file in place with corrected rows, keeping the same name and path. The stream is on delivered settings and the correction never reaches the target, so the team must say why.

option_texts.A: Rewrites arrive one batch late, because a changed file is held back for a cycle
option_texts.B: Rewrites are always ignored, because a processed name can never be revisited
option_texts.C: Rewrites are ignored by default, because changes to an input file are not picked up
option_texts.D: Rewrites need the target truncating first, because the reader compares row counts

drill_answer_short: cloudFiles.allowOverwrites defaults to false, so input directory file changes do not overwrite existing data
decision_hinge: The cloudFiles.allowOverwrites option defaults to false and controls whether to allow input directory file changes to overwrite existing data.

plausible_options.B: the correction never reaches the target

eliminated_by.A: The stream is on delivered settings
eliminated_by.D: keeping the same name and path

distractor_traps.A: T1: fabricated - there is no one-cycle delay for a changed file
distractor_traps.B: T3: confusable sibling - it is the default rather than a permanent rule, and an option changes it
distractor_traps.D: T1: fabricated - nothing compares row counts between source and target

stem: A governance lead is explaining how the platform reaches a bucket it does not own. They have to separate the object that names where the data sits from the object that holds the right to read it.

option_texts.A: An external location names the path and holds its own embedded key material
option_texts.B: A single catalog property carries both the path and the access key together
option_texts.C: A storage credential defines the path and references an external location
option_texts.D: An external location defines the path and references a storage credential

drill_answer_short: An external location defines a path plus the credentials to reach it, and those credentials live in a storage credential
decision_hinge: An external location defines a path to a cloud storage location and the credentials required to access that location, and those credentials are in turn defined in a storage credential.

plausible_options.A: separate the object that names where the data sits from the object that holds the right to read it

eliminated_by.B: the object that holds the right to read it
eliminated_by.C: explaining how the platform reaches a bucket it does not own

distractor_traps.A: T3: confusable sibling - the path object is right but the credential lives in its own securable
distractor_traps.B: T1: fabricated - no single property carries both
distractor_traps.C: T3: confusable sibling - the two roles are correct but assigned to the wrong objects

stem: A team has a pile of PDFs and images that must sit under the same permission model as the rest of the estate. They are picking the securable that exists for content which is not rows and columns.

option_texts.A: A volume, the securable that governs non-tabular data of any format
option_texts.B: An external location, which is the securable for content of any format
option_texts.C: A table, since any content can be held as rows once it is encoded
option_texts.D: A schema property, because file content is governed at the schema level

drill_answer_short: Volumes govern non-tabular data of any format, where tables govern tabular data
decision_hinge: While tables govern tabular data, volumes govern non-tabular data of any format, including structured, semi-structured, or unstructured content.

plausible_options.B: must sit under the same permission model as the rest of the estate

eliminated_by.C: a pile of PDFs and images
eliminated_by.D: the securable that exists for content which is not rows and columns

distractor_traps.B: T3: confusable sibling - an external location grants access to a path rather than governing the files as a dataset
distractor_traps.C: T5: common misconception - encoding files into rows abandons the purpose-built securable
distractor_traps.D: T1: fabricated - no schema property governs file content
